terms.label: protein serine/threonine kinase activity
terms.definition: Catalysis of the reactions: ATP + protein serine = ADP + protein serine phosphate, and ATP + protein threonine = ADP + protein threonine phosphate.

terms.label: nucleus
terms.definition: A membrane-bounded organelle of eukaryotic cells in which chromosomes are housed and replicated. In most cells, the nucleus contains all of the cell's chromosomes except the organellar chromosomes, and is the site of RNA synthesis and processing. In some species, or in specialized cell types, RNA metabolism or DNA replication may be absent.

terms.label: nucleoplasm
terms.definition: That part of the nuclear content other than the chromosomes or the nucleolus.

terms.label: DNA binding
terms.definition: Any molecular function by which a gene product interacts selectively and non-covalently with DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid).

terms.label: histone deacetylase binding
terms.definition: Binding to histone deacetylase.

terms.label: protein binding
terms.definition: Binding to a protein.

terms.label: ATP binding
terms.definition: Binding to ATP, adenosine 5'-triphosphate, a universally important coenzyme and enzyme regulator.

terms.label: negative regulation of collagen biosynthetic process
terms.definition: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of collagen, any of a group of fibrous proteins of very high tensile strength that form the main component of connective tissue in animals.

terms.label: protein-containing complex binding
terms.definition: Binding to a macromolecular complex.

terms.label: immune response
terms.definition: Any immune system process that functions in the calibrated response of an organism to a potential internal or invasive threat.

terms.label: PML body
terms.definition: A class of nuclear body; they react against SP100 auto-antibodies (PML, promyelocytic leukemia); cells typically contain 10-30 PML bodies per nucleus; alterations in the localization of PML bodies occurs after viral infection.

terms.label: negative regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II
terms.definition: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of transcription mediated by RNA polymerase II.

terms.label: positive regulation of MHC class I biosynthetic process
terms.definition: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of MHC class I.

terms.label: positive regulation of MHC class II biosynthetic process
terms.definition: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of MHC class II.

terms.label: positive regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II
terms.definition: Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of transcription from an RNA polymerase II promoter.

terms.label: regulation of DNA-templated transcription
terms.definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of cellular DNA-templated transcription.

terms.label: negative regulation of DNA-templated transcription
terms.definition: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of cellular DNA-templated transcription.

terms.label: type II interferon-mediated signaling pathway
terms.definition: The series of molecular signals initiated by interferon-gamma binding to its receptor on the surface of a target cell, and ending with the regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. transcription. Interferon gamma is the only member of the type II interferon found so far.

terms.label: protein serine kinase activity
terms.definition: Catalysis of the reactions: ATP + protein serine = ADP + protein serine phosphate.

terms.label: transcription coactivator activity
terms.definition: A transcription coregulator activity that activates or increases the transcription of specific gene sets via binding to a DNA-binding transcription factor at a specific genomic locus, either on its own or as part of a complex. Coactivators often act by altering chromatin structure and modifications. For example, one class of transcription coactivators modifies chromatin structure through covalent modification of histones. A second class remodels the conformation of chromatin in an ATP-dependent fashion. A third class modulates interactions of DNA-bound DNA-binding transcription factors with other transcription coregulators. A fourth class of coactivator activity is the bridging of a DNA-binding transcription factor to the general (basal) transcription machinery. The Mediator complex, which bridges sequence-specific DNA binding transcription factors and RNA polymerase, is also a transcription coactivator.

terms.label: transcription corepressor activity
terms.definition: A transcription coregulator activity that represses or decreases the transcription of specific gene sets via binding to a DNA-binding transcription factor at a specific genomic locus, either on its own or as part of a complex. Corepressors often act by altering chromatin structure and modifications. For example, one class of transcription corepressors modifies chromatin structure through covalent modification of histones. A second class remodels the conformation of chromatin in an ATP-dependent fashion. A third class modulates interactions of DNA-bound DNA-binding transcription factors with other transcription coregulators.

terms.label: RNA polymerase II-specific DNA-binding transcription factor binding
terms.definition: Binding to a sequence-specific DNA binding RNA polymerase II transcription factor, any of the factors that interact selectively and non-covalently with a specific DNA sequence in order to modulate transcription.

terms.label: response to type II interferon
terms.definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an interferon-gamma stimulus. Interferon-gamma is also known as type II interferon.

terms.label: response to antibiotic
terms.definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an antibiotic stimulus. An antibiotic is a chemical substance produced by a microorganism which has the capacity to inhibit the growth of or to kill other microorganisms.

terms.label: host-mediated suppression of symbiont invasion
terms.definition: A process in which a host inhibits or disrupts the entry of a symbiont into a host cell.

terms.label: DNA-binding transcription factor binding
terms.definition: Binding to a DNA-binding transcription factor, a protein that interacts with a specific DNA sequence (sometimes referred to as a motif) within the regulatory region of a gene to modulate transcription.

terms.label: RNA polymerase II general transcription initiation factor binding
terms.definition: Binding to a basal RNA polymerase II transcription factor, any of the factors involved in formation of the preinitiation complex (PIC) by RNA polymerase II and defined as a basal or general transcription factor.

terms.label: transcription coregulator binding
terms.definition: Binding to a transcription coregulator, a protein involved in regulation of transcription via protein-protein interactions with transcription factors and other transcription regulatory proteins. Cofactors do not bind DNA directly, but rather mediate protein-protein interactions between regulatory transcription factors and the basal transcription machinery.

terms.label: histone acetyltransferase activity
terms.definition: Catalysis of the reaction: L-lysyl-[histone] + acetyl-CoA = N6-acetyl-L-lysyl-[histone] + CoA + H+.

terms.label: GTP binding
terms.definition: Binding to GTP, guanosine triphosphate.

reference_identity_correction.scope: The official mouse Ciita GO:0046677 ISO assertion cites J:107465 and human P33076. That reference resolves to PMID:16280321; PMID:107465 is an unrelated cerebellar-glia study. The corrected paper measures suppression of CIITA expression after Hsp90 inhibition. The term includes gene-expression responses; the unresolved participation issue is whether the regulated CIITA product itself performs this antibiotic response.
